The work of armored assault vehicle crew members falls into four categories: vehicle driving and maneuver (driving tanks, light armored vehicles, and amphibious assault vehicles, maneuvering on land and water as training requires); weapon and onboard system operation and maintenance (operating and maintaining aiming and firing systems, operating and maintaining auxiliary weapons, including machine guns and grenade launchers); communications and navigation (operating and maintaining onboard communications and navigation equipment, keeping the crew and higher command connected and the position known); and transport and coordination (transporting personnel and equipment in combat environments and working with the crew and higher command to complete the mission). All four categories must be carried out within the unit's procedures and authorization and leave reviewable site and record evidence.

entries.answer: The official duty description is: operating tanks, light armored vehicles, and amphibious assault vehicles in land or water combat environments; the duties include driving armored vehicles that require specialized training, operating and maintaining aiming and firing systems, operating and maintaining advanced onboard communications and navigation equipment, transporting personnel and equipment in combat environments, and operating and maintaining auxiliary weapons (including machine guns and grenade launchers). Specifically, crew work includes driving armored vehicles and maneuvering per procedure, operating and maintaining aiming and firing systems and auxiliary weapons, operating and maintaining onboard communications and navigation equipment, transporting personnel and equipment in combat environments, and completing checks and records per the unit's training and operating regulations. O*NET has not published this military occupation's task list or work context data, and this page does not add daily details unsupported by sources.
entries.question: What do armored assault vehicle crew members do every day?

entries.answer: Aircraft crew members mainly operate aircraft mission systems and onboard operations; aircraft launch and recovery specialists mainly provide launch and recovery support on a ship deck or at a base; artillery and missile crew members mainly do emplacement operation and firing of artillery and missile systems; command and control center specialists mainly do information gathering and command post watch duty; infantry mainly fight in dismounted squads. The core of armored assault vehicle crew members is armored vehicle driving and maneuver, weapon and onboard system operation and maintenance, communications and navigation equipment use, and battlefield transport, and the responsibility boundaries and qualification requirements cannot be interchanged with other directions.
